Breakfast Club
At The Downs CEP School we offer a breakfast and after school club providing extra child care for parents.
The Downs CEP breakfast club has two sessions to choose from:
Session 1 runs from 7:45 – 8:35am. This session costs £4.50 per session and provides children with breakfast.
Session 2 runs from 8:15-8:35am. This session costs £3 per session and does not include breakfast.
Breakfast offers a drink which includes various juices, water and milk, and a choice of cereal, fruit, and toast. This will be varied during the term with muffins, crumpets, teacakes etc. being offered on special days.
Bookings must be made and paid for via the School Gateway App. on the 'Clubs' tab. For any cash payment, please contact the school office.
Please contact the school if you have any questions.

Personal, Social & Health Education
PSHE at The Downs allows children to find, use and share their individual voice.
The children have opportunities across our JIGSAW scheme of work to develop their understanding of the British Values and societies protected characteristics to become a well-rounded, supportive global citizen.
We develop connections to their peers, providing opportunities to discuss topics and challenge ideas in a respectful, tolerant way whilst also empowering the children to be part of our school community.

Governors
The governing board (known as the board) works collectively as a ‘whole team’, meeting six times per year, once in each term, without any separate committees. An annual planner and agenda for each meeting will include all the tasks which the board is required to consider, and the board may ‘commission’ assignments or activities arising from the business of the meeting, which will be recorded in the minutes. Any ‘commissioned’ working groups will have board drafted agreed terms of reference and will report any findings, actions, or recommended decisions to the board at its next meeting. These reports will in turn inform collective strategic decision making by the board.
In addition to ‘commissioning’ activities or actions on their behalf, the board, to ensure its core functions are fulfilled, will delegate monitoring responsibilities to ‘monitoring pairs’ or ‘individuals’. These include the Department for Education (DfE) identified as should have individual roles and those focused on the priorities of the School Plan. The board recognises the delegated monitoring individuals/pairs are replacing committees in terms of challenge, responsibility and accountability when undertaking their monitoring and reporting back to the board. The board recognises that all decisions are made by the full board and no financial delegated authority is given to monitoring pairs. Meetings of the board and delegated individuals/pairs will be considerate of the well-being of staff and executive lead/headteacher by referring to the DfE teacher workload reduction toolkit.
In each case where a function has been delegated there is a statutory duty for the delegated governor/s to report, by written monitoring reports, any findings, action or recommended decision to the board in time for its next meeting to enable informed collective strategic decision making.
The board meets at least six times a year, considers monitoring reports and recommendations, makes decisions, and conducts routine business.
Mrs Jennie Cooper and Mrs Margaret Patel are our co- Chair of Governors.
The Downs CEP School
The full governing body meets termly to discuss ways in which to support the school with their vision for improvement.

Reading and phonics
Our readers learn to enjoy, experience and escape through diverse literature. Our mission is to foster a love of reading in every child by creating a vibrant reading culture where books are valued, shared, and enrich our whole school themes. Texts are explored using phonics and our reading skills, which are embedded across all year groups, ensuring a consistent and progressive approach to reading development. Our children leave us as confident, fluent readers who can understand, question, and explore the world through words and will embrace a lifetime of learning and discovery.
The children use the reading skills cards each reading session to focus their learning and help them understand the different components of the reading journey.

Science
Science at the Downs CEP School has been developed to give the children a balance of knowledge and skills with opportunities for memorable, engaged and fun lessons. Children will be inspired by exploring real life role models and be given time to make links with their world through practical and fact-based opportunities. We aspire to allow children to make sense of the world and encourage deeper level thinking and oracy. Science naturally brings opportunities for spirituality, awe and wonder both within the classroom and in our outside spaces through the Enhanced Curriculum.
We aim to send out learning our into the world inspired to take an active interest in future social, moral and environment issues and have the knowledge and skills to make a positive impact.

Sports Premium
We receive some additional funding to support the teaching of sport but also to increase access to sporting activities. This was as a result of the Olympic Games 2012 and the desire for a sustainable legacy.
Within our school, we evaluated our own skills and knowledge of each sport and thought about the additional equipment we needed to teach these games/skills to a higher standard. For the sports that were identified by staff are requiring more support, we have employed a number of coaches over the last couple of years.
The coaches have been working alongside class teachers to enable both the children and the staff to acquire new skills and knowledge. They have also provided one-off taster days in various sports, which are designed to interest children and encourage them to pursue other sports outside of school. The sports covered thus far are: tag rugby, netball, multi skills, tchoukball, hockey, cricket, nu-age curling, dodge ball, dance, tennis and gymnastics.
